narrative_purpose: A survey plate of Pandoran fauna sensory organs — the thanator's mobile quills, the viperwolf's tapetum eyes, the direhorse's antennae, the hexapede's membrane fans — to show each animal's senses are tuned to a different perceptual niche.
subject: A four-panel naturalist study sheet of Pandoran animal heads, each emphasising its sensory apparatus: a thanator's armored skull ringed with mobile red-and-yellow sensory quills; a viperwolf's head with large green light-reflecting eyes; a direhorse's head with two long backswept mobile antennae; a hexapede's head with twin horns sheathing a thin taut membrane fan.
scene: A dark field-notebook study sheet, the four heads arranged in a grid against deep indigo, each in its own faint pool of glow.
camera: Consistent three-quarter portrait framing on each head, close and observational.
light: Cool bioluminescent rim light picking out each sensory organ; eyes catching a faint retroreflective shine; deep shadow between panels.
palette: Void-indigo ground and teal mid-tones, Pandora cyan glow on the sensory organs, scarce amber only on the thanator quills.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist study sheet, hand-painted, observed.
detail_level: High detail on each sensory structure — quills, eyes, antennae, membrane; bodies cropped out, backgrounds plain.
composition: A clean 2x2 grid of heads with dark gutters and open space around each for callout labels.
consistency_notes: Match each creature's established canon look; keep the four heads visually distinct and each ringed by dark space for labels.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
